taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes L. elapsoides was long regarded as a subspecies of L. triangulum and is now treated as a distinct species.
fieldMarks: Bright red, black and yellow bands that extend across the belly.
Snout nearly always red; red and black bands touch, red and yellow bands do not.
A coral snake has a black snout and red bands touching yellow.
behavior: Found in rotting logs and under bark in Coastal Plain pine forests; stumps and logs are common cover.
Constrictor that eats small snakes, lizards and mice.
habitat: Pine flatwoods and wet prairie hammocks; less often bottomland, mixed hardwood, upland pine, sandhills and maritime hammock.
range: Southeastern Virginia and the Coastal Plain of the Carolinas south through Georgia to southern Florida and west to eastern Louisiana, Tennessee and Kentucky.

lookalikes.name: Eastern coral snake
lookalikes.howToTell: Venomous coral snake has a black snout and red bands touching yellow; scarlet kingsnake has a red snout and red touching black.

lookalikes.name: Northern scarlet snake
lookalikes.howToTell: Scarlet snake (Cemophora coccinea) has a plain white belly; scarlet kingsnake bands cross the belly.
